D: Three out-of-work scientists open a ghost removal business in a Manhattan firehouse.
P: Crack the drinks when Ecto-1 rolls out of the firehouse for the first time.
S: green spinach and artichoke dip, corn chips for scooping
Wilt spinach, squeeze dry, chop with marinated artichokes, fold into cream cheese, sour cream, mozzarella and parmesan with garlic. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes until bubbling.
in honour of the big guy
Big marshmallows on skewers, toasted over a flame until the outside blisters. Dip in melted dark chocolate and crushed biscuits.
there's something in the fridge, and it isn't the eggs
Whip yolks with mayo, Dijon and a drop of green colouring, pipe back into whites, chives on top.
M: long enough for the whole crew
Pork and beef meatballs baked then simmered in marinara, packed into a long roll with provolone and grilled until melted.
dumplings and fried rice eaten out of the boxes on the desk
Fried rice with day-old rice, egg, lap cheong, spring onion and soy in a smoking wok. Pan-fried pork dumplings alongside.
W: giant marshmallows, toasted until they melt down
Big marshmallow toasted, sandwiched between digestive biscuits with a square of milk chocolate. Under the grill for 30 seconds if there's no fire.
K: Blitz ice with lime cordial and lemonade until slushy, a drop of green colouring.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix up to 1 day ahead, bake just before serving

steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, cool, then squeeze very dry and chop with the artichokes.
Mix the spinach and artichokes with the cream cheese, sour cream, most of the mozzarella, the parmesan and the garlic.
Spoon into a small baking dish, top with the rest of the mozzarella and bake at 190C for 20 minutes until bubbling.
Serve hot with the corn chips for scooping.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Halve the eggs and scoop the yolks into a bowl.
Whip the yolks with the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt and a drop of green food colouring until smooth.
Pipe back into the whites and scatter the chives on top.
Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl over simmering water and crush the digestive biscuits in a bag with a rolling pin.
Push 2 marshmallows onto each bamboo skewer.
Toast over a gas flame or under a hot grill, turning often, until the outside blisters.
Dip in the melted chocolate, then in the crushed biscuits, and eat while warm.

dishes.make_ahead: Meatballs and sauce up to 2 days ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Mix the pork and beef mince with the egg, parmesan, breadcrumbs, garlic, salt and pepper and roll into 16 meatballs.
Bake the meatballs on a lined tray at 200C for 15 minutes.
Simmer the passata with the oregano, add the meatballs and simmer for 15 minutes.
Split the long rolls, pack in the meatballs and sauce and lay the provolone on top.
Grill for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese has melted.

veg.make_ahead: Meatballs and sauce up to 2 days ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Fry the chopped mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat until dry and browned, then cool.
Mash the lentils roughly, then mix with the mushrooms, ricotta, egg, parmesan, breadcrumbs, garlic, salt and pepper and roll into 16 meatballs.
Bake the meatballs on a lined tray at 200C for 20 minutes until firm.
Simmer the passata with the oregano, add the meatballs and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Split the long rolls, pack in the meatballs and sauce, lay the provolone on top and grill for 2 to 3 minutes until melted.

dishes.make_ahead: Cook the rice a day ahead and chill

steps.text: Cook the jasmine rice the day before, spread it on a tray and chill overnight.
Slice the lap cheong and spring onions and beat the eggs.
Heat a wok until smoking with half the oil, scramble the eggs, then add the lap cheong, rice and 2 tbsp soy sauce and toss for 4 minutes until hot. Stir through the spring onions.
Fry the frozen pork dumplings in the rest of the oil in a frying pan for 2 minutes until the bases brown, add the water, cover and steam for 6 minutes.
Serve out of takeaway boxes with the rest of the soy sauce on the side.

veg.make_ahead: Cook the rice a day ahead and chill

steps.text: Cook the jasmine rice the day before, spread it on a tray and chill overnight.
Dice the smoked tofu, slice the spring onions and beat the eggs.

Heat a wok until smoking with half the oil and fry the tofu for 2 minutes. Push it aside, scramble the eggs, then add the rice and 2 tbsp soy sauce and toss for 4 minutes until hot. Stir through the spring onions.
Fry the frozen vegetable dumplings in the rest of the oil in a frying pan for 2 minutes until the bases brown, add the water, cover and steam for 6 minutes.
Serve out of takeaway boxes with the rest of the soy sauce on the side.
Lay 8 digestive biscuits on a tray and put a square of milk chocolate on each.
Toast the marshmallows over a flame until golden and melting, or sit one on each chocolate square and put the tray under a hot grill for 30 seconds.
Press the remaining biscuits on top and eat straight away.
Blitz the ice with the lime cordial and lemonade until slushy.
Add a drop of green food colouring and blitz again.
Pour into 4 glasses and add a slice of lime to each.

edition.cue: Serve the takeaway boxes when the team settles in at the firehouse.

s.note: Hot spinach and artichoke dip baked bubbling under mozzarella, green as Slimer, with crisp corn chips for scooping.
s.how: Thaw 150g frozen spinach and squeeze very dry. Chop 150g drained marinated artichokes. Mix with 150g cream cheese, 100g sour cream, 75g grated mozzarella and 1 crushed garlic clove. Spoon into a small baking dish, top with 25g mozzarella and bake at 190°C for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling. Serve with 200g corn chips.

s.note: Oven-crisp chicken wings tossed in buttery hot sauce, served with cool ranch for the firehouse crew.
s.how: Pat 800g separated chicken wings dry. Toss with 1 tsp baking powder (not bicarbonate), 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp smoked paprika. Spread on a rack over a lined tray and roast at 220°C for 40 to 45 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and at least 74°C in the thickest part. Mix 40ml hot sauce with 30g melted butter and toss with wings. Serve with 100ml ranch; leave some wings unsauced for a milder option.

m.note: Sticky sesame chicken, wok-fried egg rice and blistered broccoli. Serve in takeaway boxes.
m.how: Cut 600g boneless chicken thighs into bite-size pieces, toss with 3 tbsp cornflour and shallow-fry in batches until crisp and at least 74°C inside. Drain. Mix 2 tbsp each soy sauce and honey, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves and 60ml water. Simmer, thicken with 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water, then toss through chicken and 1 tbsp sesame seeds. Fry 2 beaten eggs in 1 tbsp oil; add 500g chilled cooked rice, 2 sliced spring onions and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Stir-fry until piping hot. Char 1 head broccoli in a hot pan with 1 tbsp oil and a splash of water. Divide everything into 4 takeaway boxes.

w.note: Fudgy chocolate brownie baked in a skillet, buried under toasted marshmallows and served warm with vanilla ice cream.
w.how: Melt 100g butter with 100g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whisk in 120g caster sugar and 2 eggs, then fold in 60g plain flour, 15g cocoa and a pinch of salt. Pour into a buttered 20cm ovenproof skillet or baking dish. Bake at 180°C for 20 to 25 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is fudgy. Top with 100g marshmallows and grill briefly until golden, watching closely. Serve with 400ml vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Orange, lime and lemonade, blended with ice. Suspiciously green. Completely drinkable.
d.how: Blend 300ml orange juice, juice of 2 limes, 300ml lemonade and 400g ice until slushy. Add a tiny drop of green food colouring if wanted. Divide into 4 glasses and serve immediately.
